why: the batch's sitrep items report events happening to works rather than a first build, so the progress-report gate and the what-happened gate blur.

why.T3-041: The bag's concepts propose and build additions to the room's existing road — Mario Kart characters, prisms, endings, revivals and extensions of strands — i.e. the room extending its own work rather than proposing a first mark (T3-033) or only calling hands (T3-002).

why.T3-021: The concepts call to preserve and maintain the deteriorating LEGO logo ('we must preserve it', 'Help Maintain The Logo', 'sacred task to preserve') — keeping the work intact, i.e. watching and repairing rather than fighting a named attacker (T3-005) or weighing upkeep against expansion (T3-042).

why.T3-054: Members carry the road to successor canvases (placetwo, pxls.space) and plan the next road; the keepsake and identity posts are commemoration, not a later canvas, so the new-canvas act leads.

why.T3-014: Members set up and name the room's Discord, post invites and send each other into #place to coordinate — moving planning into a chat.
why.T3-002: Members also call the room's own members to come and place the Skyrim logo ('Help us complete the Skyrim logo', get to r/place) with no chat in the ask.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-014's gate covers sending members into the Discord chat for plans but not the open calls for hands to come and place the logo, which are T3-002's gate; a single T3-014 placement would drop the 'calling people in' half.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C0912502 'Help us complete the Skyrim logo in r/place', C1417211 'Help us have create /r/skyrim... Every pixel helps' and C0190184's rally to finish the artwork are calls to the room's own members to come and place.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: Drop T3-002 if forced to one; the Discord routing is the larger and more distinctive act, but the open recruitment calls would be lost.

why.T3-035: The bag's concepts are outsiders petitioning the road, which holds space, for room and permission to build ('permission to build Master Chief below Helix?', 'requesting permission to use a 14x16 px space') — asking a host for space rather than granting it (T3-012) or settling a mutual border (T3-010).

why.T3-038: Members post situation reports and status checks on the canvas and the road's progress ('the rainbow forces are making progress in blue-country', 'Top left sitrep', 'Kirby! Recovery from OSU') — reporting the work's state rather than tracing a culprit (T3-087) or a post-close account (T3-073).

why.T3-188: An organised room tells others that rogue shards, unsanctioned expansions and hivemind placers acting in its name are not under its control ('the expansion in blue is not officially sanctioned by us', 'the shard under the trans flag is not part of the official rainbow road', 'this is just the normal damage... of the hivemind').

why.T3-010: The concepts settle where the road's path meets neighbours' art — bounces, weaves, portals, mergers and requests to go around or under (Bitcoin, the sanctioned trans-flag weave, Mona Lisa) — lines and space worked out with neighbours rather than a rival's work destroyed (T3-006) or the mark's own design argued (T3-004).

why.T3-038: Same reporting theme as position 6: situation reports and status checks on the canvas and the road's progress, reporting the work's state rather than tracing a culprit (T3-087) or a post-close account (T3-073).

why.T3-009: The concepts celebrate and praise the road's finished and continuing work ('Look at our beautiful rainbow shoot into existence!', 'We did it!!!!', 'the glory of the rainbow road') — marking the room's work as achieved rather than mourning it (T3-029) or crediting makers (T3-043).

why.T3-046: Members argue whether the road's covering and expansion over others' art is right ('focus on creating rather than destroying', 'We care not for petty rivalries', complaints the road is eating the US flag) — the fairness of covering argued, not a design settled (T3-004) or the canvas judged worthless (T3-037).
